title: How the brain copes with bad times
content:
by Joshua L. Gowin, Colleen M. Sheller

A unifying framework of the brain’s representation and manipulation of negative emotional experiences has been elusive. A new study in PLOS Biology describes how different brain systems correspond to emotion regulation and suggests a key dimension that explains how we feel. How does the brain represent and manipulate negative emotional experiences? This Primer explores a new study in PLOS Biology that describes how different brain systems correspond to emotion regulation and suggests a key dimension that explains how we feel.
author: Joshua L. Gowin
